items.title: Wayne Bergeron interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 29, 2020
items.q: Whereas now we have Doc Severinsen at 93 years old who can still hit a high G.

ctx.x: Wasn’t a big part of his success as a trumpet player having something to do with his breathing?

Yeah. I mean he talked about, you know, the yoga breath and things he learned in India, and which Bobby Shew teaches as well. And Bobby Shew kind of learned these things from him. So I would say yes. But Maynard was doing that long before he learned how to do that. I mean Maynard was playing unbelievably efficient way before he learned about Eastern philosophy and different kinds of breathing. I mean I think it enhanced his playing later and made him even more efficient. And Bobby Shew, you know, teaches a thing…

be known, I think Bobby Shew is the greatest brass educator in a hundred years. Because, you know, us trumpet players and brass players, we kind of have our heads stuck in the sand of tradition and that’s Bobby’s line. You’ve got your head stuck in the sand of tradition. When you’re looking at these books and concepts from over a hundred years ago, you know, things around the turn of the century, you know of the 1900s, of how we played the trumpet or the cornet at the time. And we’re still trying to apply those…
